data.title: China Industrial Production Growth Rises
data.description:
BEIJING (dpa-AFX) - China's industrial production growth accelerated in August but retail sales registered a weaker expansion, data from the National Bureau of Statistics showed Tuesday.

Industrial production increased 5.2 percent on a yearly basis in August, faster than the 4.5 percent rise in July. The annual growth also exceeded forecast of 4.8 percent.

Retail sales grew only 0.4 percent from the last year. This was slower than the 0.6 percent growth seen in July and economists' forecast of 0.8 percent.

During January to August, fixed asset investment declined 7.2 percent from the same period last year and also matched expectations.

ING economist Lynn Song said weak Chinese consumption and investment persisted amid soft domestic demand, while solid external demand continues to support industrial activity.

Overall, the third-quarter GDP looks likely to stay near or below the low-end of the target range of around 4.5 percent to 5 percent, the economist added.

data.title: ZAWYA: Oman's real estate market value hits over $4bln in July
data.description:
By Staff Writer

The value of real estate transactions in the Sultanate of Oman recorded a 7.7 percent increase in July 2026, reaching OMR 1.7157 billion , compared to OMR 1.593 billion during the same period in 2025.

According to data issued by the National Media Center, the value of real estate transactions rose by 15.7 percent to OMR 843.2 million , compared to OMR 728.5 million during the same period in 2025. The number of sales contracts also increased by 3.9 percent, reaching 39,719 contracts, compared to 38,226 contracts.

The value of mortgage contracts also recorded an increase of 0.7 percent , reaching OMR 864.4 million, compared to OMR 858.4 million during the same period in 2025. The number of mortgage contracts rose by 22.3 percent, reaching 15,441 contracts, compared to 12,621 contracts.

The value of swap contracts continued its upward trend, increasing by OMR 33.6 million to reach OMR 8.2 million by July 2026, compared to OMR 6.1 million during the same period in 2025. Meanwhile, the number of swap contracts increased by approximately 41.6 percent, reaching 411 contracts, compared to 704 contracts.

Regarding real estate ownership, the number of issued properties increased by 10.7 percent , reaching 119,832 by the end of July 2026, compared to 134,206 properties during the same period in 2025. The number of units issued to citizens of the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) countries also increased by 11.2 percent , reaching 643 properties, compared to 724.

data.title: SpaceX's first Starfall customer is European mission integrator Space Cargo
data.description:
By Joey Roulette

SpaceX's new Starfall business of returning products and other payloads from Earth's orbit has signed a mission deal with integrator Space Cargo as the unit's first customer, the company's Chief Executive Nicolas Gaume told Reuters.

Space Cargo aims to fly in 2028 an orbital reentry flight on the first commercial mission of Starship, which will deploy SpaceX's Starfall - a disk-shaped capsule designed to carry materials on short trips through orbit and back to Earth.

Launched aboard Falcon 9 and eventually Starship, Starfall is an aluminum housing protected by a 10-foot (3-m) -wide heatshield that SpaceX offers to customers seeking to make products or do research in the microgravity of space.

Luxembourg-based Space Cargo will place its "BentoBox" system in the Starfall capsule, positioning itself as an integrator in the SpaceX program with plans to book more such future missions, Space Cargo CEO Gaume said.

"We're flying 200 kilos with our current systems, but with Starship and Starfall, we're going to go to ton and tons" of customer payloads, "and that’s really what we want," he added.

The box would secure up to 1 ton of different types of payloads from Space Cargo's own customers that it signed up for the mission, allowing them to survive reentry and be safely returned to Earth for commercial use.

The Space Cargo deal is the first known customer for SpaceX's Starfall program, which emerged quickly earlier this year before demonstrating a capsule mission in June.

The product's central capability is its heatshield, a commodification of SpaceX's experience ferrying its larger Dragon capsules between Earth and space mainly for NASA.

The first BentoBox on a Starfall capsule will be among payloads on SpaceX's first commercial mission with Starship, SpaceX's giant next-generation rocket under development, Gaume said.

That mission is planned for 2028, Space Cargo said in a statement.

SpaceX, which did not respond to a request for comment, has not previously said when Starship will fly its first commercial mission.

The emerging business of returning payloads from space is valuable for customers such as drugmakers relying on the microgravity of space for research and production involving higher purities impossible to attain in Earth's gravity.

There are unique benefits of in-space production of other products, such as fiber optic cables, which are of higher quality when produced in microgravity on the International Space Station, NASA has said.

Nearly half Space Cargo's potential customers for its first Starfall mission are in the life sciences and biotechnology sectors, the company said.

The Starfall program joins a growing industry of capsule reentry services, where SpaceX faces rivalry from smaller startups such as California-based Varda Space, whose flagship capsule has flown 6 missions and lands in an Australian desert.

The Pentagon has seen capsule reentry missions, which must aerodynamically steer through the blazing-hot hypersonic speeds of atmospheric reentry, as useful for research and tests involving hypersonic weapons and as potential target practice for its Golden Dome missile defense program.

Gaume said flying its BentoBox with Starship and Starfall promises a fast pace of missions as SpaceX targets an unprecedented Starship flight rate once the rocket emerges from development.

BentoBox has plans to fly with other capsules, such as German startup ATMOS Space Cargo's Phoenix craft and the European Space Agency's Space Rider.

"It's really the volume and the rhythm" that makes the Starfall deal key, added Gaume, who declined to detail pricing and costs.

Starship is nearing routine flights but its development has been years behind schedule.

Its next text flight sometime this year, the 14th since 2023, will seek to put its first SpaceX-built Starlink satellites in orbit, followed by increasingly frequent in-house satellite launches that have come to dominate SpaceX's schedule.

The 2028 target for Starship's first commercial mission suggests several of the rocket's first flights throughout 2027 will serve SpaceX's Starlink satellite unit, and possibly its Starmind business of putting AI data centers in space if those satellites are ready in time.

data.title: Hitting Brakes on AI Would Refocus Markets on Gloom — Market Talk
data.description: Slower model development will undoubtedly slow AI investment, which by some estimates, accounted for around half of U.S. economic growth in 1H of 2025, says Ipek Ozkardeskaya, senior analyst at Swissquote. At a time when the Western world needs AI-led growth to keep its head above water, the impact could be significant, she adds. Trade tensions, wars, disrupted trade routes, spiking energy prices, rising inflationary pressures and rising borrowing costs could only be neutralized by AI, she adds. Hitting the brakes could provide a negative backdrop for cyclical sectors, particularly industrials and consumer discretionary, she says. (james.glynn@wsj.com; @JamesGlynnWSJ)

data.title: Indian bonds sink as RBI plans ₹1 lakh crore sales to drain liquidity
data.description:
Indian bonds declined after the central bank said it would sell sovereign notes to drain cash from lenders, adding to the supply of debt in a year when the market is already under pressure from record government borrowing.

Yields on the 6.94 per cent bond due 2036 rose by 7 basis points to 7.09 per cent, while those on the 6.36 per cent note due 2031 climbed 16 basis points to 6.78 per cent, as domestic bonds joined a global sell-off. Indian markets were closed on Monday for a public holiday.

The Reserve Bank of India late Friday said it would drain ₹1 lakh crore ($10.5 billion) from lenders through bond sales, its strongest effort yet to soak up surplus cash in the banking system that poses inflationary risks. The additional supply is worsening the bond-market outlook just as high oil prices stoke inflation risks and raise the chances of an RBI interest-rate hike next month. Federal borrowing of close to ₹8 lakh crore is lined up over the next six months, when bond sales by provinces are typically heavy.

“The decision is the most stringent action the RBI has taken so far and the logical casualty has been the five-year segment, which was richly valued,” said VRC Reddy, Head of Treasury at Karur Vysya Bank Ltd. “I expect the yield curve to steepen further as short-end yields climb,” he said, adding the gap between the five- and 10-year yield may stabilise around 20-30 basis points.

India’s inflation climbed in August, moving closer to the top of the central bank’s 2-6 per cent target range. With price pressures rising, Citigroup Inc. said it expects the RBI to raise borrowing costs by 50-75 basis points, with the tightening cycle starting next month.

The RBI’s bond sales will be carried out in three tranches, with the first one due on September 17. In that auction, the central bank will sell notes maturing in about three to six years.

data.title: ZAWYA: Emaar Misr signs over $271mln contracts with Rowad, Innovo for Marassi Red Sea
data.description:
By Staff Writer

Real estate developer Emaar Misr has signed two construction contracts totaling EGP 14 billion with Rowad Modern Engineering and Innovo Group for the Infinity Beach and Island Living projects at Marassi Red Sea, as per an emailed press release.

The agreements bring the total value of construction contracts awarded for the development to approximately EGP 20 billion, representing one of the largest construction investments in Emaar Misr’s history. The company plans to accelerate work on the first phase, with unit handovers scheduled for 2029.

Under the first contract, Egypt-based turnkey contractor Rowad Modern Engineering will build 675 villas and townhouses at Infinity Beach, spanning a total built-up area of approximately 150,000 square meters.

Innovo Group will construct approximately 220 villas at Island Living, covering a built-up area of around 100,000 square meters.

Construction has also begun on the Marina buildings under an earlier contract with Arabian Construction Company (ACC). The phase comprises 32 residential buildings with 750 units across approximately 100,000 square meters.

Emaar Misr’s portfolio spans West and East Cairo, the North Coast, and the Red Sea region. Its developments include Marassi, Soul, Belle Vie, Cairo Gate, Uptown Cairo, Mivida, Mivida Gardens in New Cairo, and Marassi Red Sea.

data.title: ZAWYA: Egypt’s ICT sector growth accelerates to 13.8% in FY2024/25: IDSC
data.description:
By Staff Writer

Egypt’s Information and Communications Technology (ICT) sector recorded a real growth rate at fixed prices of 13.76% during fiscal year (FY) 2024/2025, compared to 8.43% in FY2013/2014, according to a report by the Information and Decision Support Center (IDSC).

The report also highlighted strong growth in Egypt’s digital exports, which rose by 7.2% year-on-year (YoY) to $7.4 billion in 2025 from $6.9 billion.

Outsourcing services exports reached $5.2 billion in 2025, higher than $2.4 billion in 2022 and $4.3 billion in 2024. The figure more than doubled over three years, with outsourcing exports targeted to hit $6 billion in 2026.

Moreover, IDSC pointed out that the ICT sector continued to attract higher public investment, as its value rose from EGP 750 million in FY2013/2014 to EGP 27.69 billion in FY2024/2025.

As for the telecommunications and internet user base, the number of mobile phone subscriptions reached 125.65 million lines in March 2026, marking an annual growth of 8.47% from 115.83 million.

Active mobile internet subscriptions increased by 9.48% to 94.43 million in March 2026 from 86.25 million a year earlier. High-speed fixed internet subscriptions also rose to 12.95 million from 11.87 million during the same period.

Regarding investments, public investment in the ICT sector surged from EGP 750 million in FY2013/2014 to about EGP 27.69 billion in FY2024/2025.
